REGULAR MEETING AGENDA

CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT:

  Bill Ihrke, City Attorney, provided the following Closed Session report:

  ITEM 12C:

  The City Council received a status update on the case entitled City of Whittier et al. v.
  Superior Court of Los Angeles County et al., Los Angeles County Superior Court case no.
  23 STCP 03579, transferred to Orange County Superior Court with the same case number
  (“City of Whittier”). The complaint was filed by the City of Whittier and many other cities
  in Los Angeles County, including City of Cerritos as a Co-Plaintiff/Petitioner, challenging
  the Los Angeles County Superior Court’s recently adopted Misdemeanor and Felony Bail
  Schedules, with the case seeking declaratory and injunctive relief and/or writ of mandate
  to enjoin the implementation of the Bail Schedules. The substance of the case may be
  summarized as challenging what is commonly referred to a “zero-bail” or “no bail” system,
  and more specifically summarized as alleged in Paragraph 29 of the Complaint:
  “Defendants failed to satisfy their mandatory duties as to setting of bail” because the
  recently adopted Bail Schedules “impose a blanket lifting of whole swaths of categories
  from being bailable offenses, and requires only citation and release, or booking and
  release, as to blanket categories of offenses – with no detention or individualized
  evaluations or assessments of particular crimes or individuals.”

  On December 11, 2023, the trial court denied the Plaintiffs’ Motion for a Preliminary
  Injunction and Granted Defendants’ Demurrer with leave to amend the Complaint. The
  trial court concluded, in part, that the City of Whittier case is related to another pending
  case relating to the Los Angeles County Superior Court Bail Schedules, Urquidi v. City of
  Los Angeles, L.A. Superior Court Case No. 22STCP04044 (“Urquidi”), and concluded that
  an appropriate remedy for the cities in the City of Whittier case is to intervene in the
  Urquidi case.

  Based on the discussion by City Council and advice provided by the City’s special counsel,
  Jones & Mayer, in the City of Whittier case, the following actions were taken:
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, January 11, 2024, 7:00 p.m.
